patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches place branding/navigation at the very top as a persistent header area separated from the rest of the page content; the desktop sketch especially shows a compact top bar above the hero, implying it remains available while scrolling.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header/navigation should stay fixed or become fixed on scroll so primary navigation remains accessible across the long page.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear whether the nav is always fixed from page load or only becomes sticky after scrolling past an initial offset.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile layout omits visible horizontal navigation links and reserves only stacked content, strongly implying a collapsed mobile navigation control rather than full inline nav.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A hamburger button should toggle the mobile navigation panel open/closed, likely as an overlay or slide-in drawer.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw the icon or reveal whether the menu opens full-screen, from the side, or as a dropdown.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop header shows multiple short nav items spaced horizontally, a common sketch convention for top-level navigation categories that likely expose deeper links.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Top-level nav items should reveal submenus on hover and/or click, with support for keyboard activation.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly depict submenu panels, so submenu depth and trigger mode are inferred rather than shown.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include a contact-style form with multiple text inputs, a select field, a large message textarea, and a submit button.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Required fields should be validated before submission, with inline errors and submission-state feedback. Email/phone formatting may also need validation depending on field rules.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not indicate which fields are required or whether validation is inline, on blur, or on submit.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show one form field with a downward chevron, indicating a dropdown/select control distinct from plain text inputs.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If styled beyond the native browser select, it needs JS for open/close state, selected option display, and keyboard interaction; otherwise native select behavior may suffice.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch alone cannot confirm whether this is a native select or a custom-styled combobox.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a fairly simple marketing/content page with the main JavaScript concentrated in navigation and the contact form rather than dynamic content modules. Cross-viewport differences are important: desktop suggests exposed top navigation with likely dropdowns, while mobile suggests collapsed navigation behind a hamburger. The form appears in both views and is the clearest explicit interaction area, requiring validation and select-state handling. No strong evidence appears for tabs, accordions, modals, toasts, infinite scroll, or load-more behavior.
